title: Outlive
author: Peter Attia, with Bill Gifford
blurb: Physician Peter Attia argues that modern medicine is good at treating acute illness but too slow to prevent the chronic diseases that actually kill most of us. He calls these the Four Horsemen: heart disease, cancer, neurodegenerative disease like Alzheimer's, and metabolic dysfunction such as type 2 diabetes. Each one builds silently for decades, so he urges a proactive, personalized approach he calls Medicine 3.0. The goal is not just more years but better ones, extending healthspan as well as lifespan. His most powerful tool is exercise, including aerobic fitness, strength and stability, trained deliberately for the life you want at 90. He adds nutrition, sleep and, finally, emotional health, drawing on his own painful journey to show that longevity matters only if the life is worth living.

lessons.b: Your last decade of life is often spent in decline, and the real goal is to extend healthspan, the years you live with a capable body and mind, not just lifespan.
issues: scene 4: The 'INDEPENDENCE' label overflows the amber puzzle piece. Its first letters run into the left knob cut-out and touch the piece outline, so text overlaps the shape edge. (fix: Shrink the label or widen the piece, then centre the text inside the solid body of the piece with at least 16px padding from the knob cut-outs. Alternatively, place the label below the piece.)

scene 0: The 'OR' label between the two figures is tiny, well under 18px at 1600 width. The two figures are also small and hard to read: the hiking figure's pole reads as a walking cane. (fix: Enlarge the figures by about 1.5x. Raise the 'OR' label to at least 20px. Make the active figure clearly hiking, e.g. mid-stride with a backpack, instead of standing with a cane-like stick.)

lessons.b: Standard medicine waits for disease to appear and then treats it, while Attia's Medicine 3.0 aims to prevent illness early with care tailored to each person.
Heart disease, cancer, neurodegenerative disease and metabolic dysfunction cause most deaths, develop silently over decades, and must be tackled long before symptoms appear.

lessons.t: Exercise Is the Strongest Longevity Drug
lessons.b: Aerobic fitness, built through steady Zone 2 training and pushing up your VO2 max, is one of the strongest predictors of how long and how well you live.
